title: Delete the Middle of a List
statement: `head` is the head of a linked list with `n` nodes. Delete the **middle node**, which is the node at position `floor(n / 2)` counting from `0` (for 6 nodes it is the 4th node; for 5 nodes it is the 3rd). Return the head of the list. A list with one node becomes empty; an empty list stays empty.

examples.explanation: n = 6, so position 3 (the value 16) is removed.
The only node is the middle one.

hints.nudge: You do not know n in advance. If one pointer moves twice as fast as another, where is the slow one when the fast one reaches the end?
hints.pattern: Slow and fast pointers, keeping a pointer to the node BEFORE the slow one so that you can unlink it.
hints.pseudocode:
if head is empty or has one node: return empty
prev = none; slow = head; fast = head
while fast and fast.next: prev = slow; slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next
prev.next = slow.next
return head
hints.walkthrough: Counting the nodes first and then walking to the middle takes two passes. With two pointers one pass is enough: `fast` moves two steps for each step of `slow`, so when fast reaches the end, slow is at position floor(n / 2), the middle in the problem's sense. To delete it you need the node before it, so remember it (`prev`) as slow moves. Then prev.next = slow.next. A list with one node is a special case (there is no node before the middle): the result is empty. O(n) time, O(1) memory.
